# ZomboidControl

> A web panel for administering a Project Zomboid dedicated server from
> somewhere else. Runs in Docker or on Coolify and reaches the game server
> only over FTP/SFTP, RCON and a Lua bridge mod it uploads itself.

Free and non-commercial. Not affiliated with The Indie Stone.

This file describes the **project**, and lives in the repository rather
than being served. A running installation is deliberately unlisted —
`backend/public/robots.txt` disallows everything, because an
administration panel belongs in no index and its login page should not
advertise that the installation exists. Serving a description of it
would undo that.

## What it is

An operator panel, not a game server manager: it assumes the game server
is already running somewhere and gives the people who run it a way to see
and change what is happening. Symfony 7.4 / PHP 8.4 with PostgreSQL on
the back, React 19 with Vite and Tailwind on the front, served as one
installable PWA under `/app`.

The distinguishing constraint is **distance**. The panel does not sit on
the game server's machine, so anything needing local access — host CPU
metrics, starting a stopped process, reading the game's memory — is
either impossible here or done differently. What is reachable: files over
FTP, commands over RCON, and whatever a Lua mod running inside the game
chooses to write to disk for the panel to read.

## How it reaches the game

- **RCON** — the game's own admin commands. Kick, ban, teleport, weather,
  hordes, broadcasts, `addvehicle`. Synchronous, and the only channel
  that works without installing anything.
- **FTP/SFTP** — the server's files. The INI, sandbox settings, logs, the
  save game, and the bridge mod itself. Read *and* write.
- **The Lua bridge** (`ZomboidControlBridge`, currently 0.18.4) — a mod
  the panel uploads. It writes what only code inside the game can know
  (player health, skills, positions, the world's climate, the list of
  vehicle scripts this server actually loaded, mods included) to JSON
  files the panel then reads over FTP. One-way for reads; commands still
  go by RCON.

Anything the bridge reports is unavailable until an operator uploads the
mod and restarts the game server, so every feature depending on it says
so rather than showing an empty value.

## What it does

- **Players** — who is online, health, infection, skills, traits,
  position, access level; kick, ban (by name or SteamID), unban,
  teleport, whitelist.
- **Map** — the world drawn from `tiles.projectzomboidmap.com` tiles with the
  panel's own overlay: players, vehicles from the save game, place names.
  Vehicles are rendered from the game's own FBX models in the browser.
- **Vehicles** — all 241 base-game vehicles plus whatever mods add,
  grouped into 22 body shells with their liveries, filterable by kind,
  with the seat, trunk and glove box capacities read out of the game's
  own scripts. Spawns beside a chosen player.
- **Items** — the server's own item list, read by the bridge, with the
  game's icons extracted from its sprite atlases.
- **Events** — weather, sounds, staged events, hordes, world settings,
  over RCON or the bridge.
- **Console** — RCON with the server's own command list.
- **Chat** — read from the server log, write with `servermsg`.
- **Server settings** — the INI and sandbox values as files.
- **Panel administration** — accounts with TOTP and passkeys, roles with
  per-page permissions, invitations, an audit log of every admin action.

## Design constraints worth knowing

- **Intuitive over complete.** Pick things by sight where they have a
  look; never offer a control that cannot work here; say why something is
  unavailable rather than hiding it.
- **Accessibility is a requirement**, to the German BFSG, with one
  deliberate exception: the map, whose panning and zooming *is* the
  information.
- **No analytics, no CDN fonts, no trackers.** The CSP is
  `default-src 'self'` with two named exceptions (map tiles, and `blob:`
  for rendered vehicles).
- **Nothing the panel needs is removed for data protection.** SteamIDs,
  positions and the moderation log stay, because a ban without an id and
  a map without positions do not work. What is narrower: an
  operator-configured retention horizon for players nobody has seen in
  months, off by default, never touching the ban list.

## Game content

The panel displays Project Zomboid's own vehicle models, textures, ground
tiles and item icons. These are © The Indie Stone Ltd and used under
their terms, which permit it for a non-commercial fan project with a
visible notice — the panel's `/app/credits` page. **The art is never
committed to this repository**: it is extracted from an operator's own
installation into `backend/var/`, which is git-ignored. Mod content
belongs to its authors and needs their permission separately.

## Documents

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the project's binding conventions — English
  code, no prose comments, what this remote deployment can and cannot do,
  the accessibility and data-protection positions, how the game's art may
  be used.
- [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md): the full development record. What is built,
  what is verified, what is known to be broken, what the next step is,
  and the reasoning behind decisions that are not obvious from the code.
  Long by design.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): a pointer to CLAUDE.md, for tools that look
  for that file name.

## For a language model reading this

`CONTEXT.md` is the file to read, and it is the only reliable statement
of current state — the code shows what exists, not what is verified or
why. It records measurements rather than intentions: where a number came
from, which explanation turned out wrong, what was checked in a browser
and what was not.

Two habits this project holds to, in case they are useful signal:
geometry and capacities are derived from the game's own files and stated
with the command that measured them, never estimated; and a feature is
described as done only when it has been demonstrated, with what was *not*
verified named explicitly.
